research_question: How have individual difference variables been represented in empirical research on sourcing (readers' use of information about a text's origin, authorship, or context when comprehending or evaluating written resources), how are these individual differences related to sourcing outcomes, and do the relationships between individual differences and sourcing vary with how sourcing is measured or with the domain or topic of the reading materials? (Compiled from the review's four stated research questions.)
inclusion_criteria: The studies should examine the comprehension or evaluation of written resources, either text alone or text in combination with other representations.
The studies should report empirical research (e.g., no reviews or theoretical papers were included).

The studies should include actual reading; survey studies in which participants were asked to rank the trustworthiness of different types of media outlets in general without reading texts from these outlets were not included.
The studies should include at least one individual difference variable and one measure of sourcing.
The studies should examine typically developed populations (e.g., no participants with learning disabilities).
The studies should have a quantitative design and report results through numerical data.
The studies should be published in English.
exclusion_criteria: No relevant variables measured: no individual-difference variable or sourcing measure relevant to the review.
Incorrect population, e.g. not a typically developed population.
Incorrect publication type, e.g. a review or theoretical paper rather than an empirical primary study.
Incorrect language, i.e. not published in English.

notes: Eligibility criteria and research question of the Anmarkrud et al. (2021) review; the protocol is withdrawn and unused. The SYNERGY+ metadata's publication.eligibility_criteria (read-only upstream cache, not part of this repository) gives the same seven inclusion criteria word for word. The open-access article PDF (Springer, CC BY, OpenAlex primary_location.pdf_url https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s10648-021-09640-7.pdf, accessed 2026-09-06) supplies the page references and the exclusion reasons the metadata omits. Research question compiled from the four research questions stated in the Introduction, PDF pages 8-9 (article pp. 756-757): RQ1 'To what extent have the individual difference factors highlighted within conceptualizations of multiple document representation and use been included in the empirical research on sourcing?'; RQ2 'To what extent have proposed relationships between individual differences and sourcing been supported by the empirical research?'; RQ3 'Are there any indications that relationships between individual differences and sourcing may vary with the way sourcing is measured?'; RQ4 '... may vary with the domain or topic addressed in the reading materials?'. Inclusion criteria 1-7 are transcribed from 'Study Selection and Data Extraction' (article pp. 757-758, PDF pages 9-10), 'To be eligible for the review, the studies had to fulfill the following inclusion criteria', which matches the metadata eligibility_criteria string exactly; all seven are marked source=paper and derived=false, quoted near-verbatim. exclusion_criteria are the abstract-screening exclusion reasons stated in 'Results' (article p. 758, PDF page 10): 'Of the 2891 records that were screened, 2618 were removed from the review for the following reasons: no relevant variables measured (1672 records), incorrect study design (430 records), incorrect population (193 records), incorrect publication type (316 records), or incorrect language (7 records).' These five reasons are coarser than the seven inclusion criteria (several inclusion criteria share one abstract-screening bucket); the review's own full-text exclusion reasons, a separate six-category breakdown of the 252 full-text exclusions on the same page, are not used because exclusion_criteria describe the title and abstract screening decision, matching label_field. All five are marked source=paper, page 758, derived=false because they are the review's own stated categories, not negations. exclusion_criteria E1-E5 carry the reason categories only, never the review's realized counts or a rank claim, because _build_screening_prompt (backend/app/agents/relevance_screener_agent.py) renders exclusion_criteria verbatim to the screener before it reads a record and the counts would disclose the review's outcome distribution; the counts live in criteria_provenance.exclusion[i].location as audit evidence that never reaches the model. The article's own header shows the print-issue year as 2022 ('Educational Psychology Review (2022) 34:749-792') although OpenAlex and Crossref record 2021-10-29 as the online publication date and the SYNERGY dataset id uses 2021; both years are recorded in source_review. label_field = label_abstract_screening because the evaluated task is title-and-abstract screening; primary_label = label_included per protocols/README.md's 'Choosing the primary label and label_field' section. n_records (2284) and n_label_included (64) are the catalogue figures in dataset_source; no labels file is cached for this dataset, so no fetch file and no hydration exist for it. Record order: run_screening.py shuffles the records deterministically before batching (random.Random('<dataset>:20260902'), recorded as record_order_seed in the run meta); this protocol does not change that (see protocols/README.md).
